title: CT Scan Scheduling and Intravenous Contrast Protocol
content: CT scans requiring intravenous (IV) contrast must be preceded by a serum creatinine test to assess renal function; patients with creatinine above 1.5 mg/dL require Radiology Physician sign-off before contrast administration. Scheduling must be done through the HIS Radiology Module by the requesting department, with at least 2 hours' notice for routine scans and immediate priority for emergency cases. Patients must be nil-by-mouth (NPO) for 4 hours prior to contrast CT; nursing staff must verify and document NPO compliance before sending the patient to Radiology. The Radiology Technologist must confirm allergy history (especially iodine/shellfish) and obtain written consent for contrast use. Any adverse contrast reactions must be reported immediately to the Radiology Attending and documented in the patient's HIS record.
